Prevention: Deep ploughing to a depth of 20 cm when destroying crop residues.
Avoid mechanical damage that may be caused by insects and birds if possible because it helps entry of disease in the cob.
Hot water treatment of seed: 52°C (when the water is hot but you can still put your finger in) for 8 minutes.
Monitoring: Crop should be visited twice a week from early silking stage to 2-3 weeks after silking.
Look for whitish powdery-like material on corn grains.

The whitish powder can be observed by removing the husk of the cob.
Apply control measures when 10 out of 100 ears are damaged and a quarter of the cob is infected.
Check for insect damage to ears which can cause disease to develop and check for the stalk rot phase of this disease which can occur before the ears get diseased.
Direct Control: Very early removal of infected cobs (do not feed to livestock) to remove disease from the field.
Hot water treatment of seeds at 50°C (hot but bearable for the hand) for 10 minutes before sowing will help kill the pathogen.
Harvest at around 25% moisture and dry to 15% moisture within 24-48 hours for shelled corn to minimise kernel damage and field losses.
Restrictions: Make sure you wear protective clothing such as gloves, and a mask when using chemicals.
Do not smoke or eat when applying chemicals.
